items.description_text: In this session, Centurion Channel members discuss strategies for boosting e-commerce growth through TikTok marketing, off-Amazon advertising channels, and the integration of AI in business operations. TOPICS: TikTok strategy and content creation for e-commerce products Off-Amazon advertising and affiliate marketing approaches Practical applications of AI in e-commerce businesses
cliff_notes:
In this session Centurion Channel Members discuss strategies for e-commerce growth with an emphasis on marketing via TikTok utilizing off-Amazon advertising, and harnessing AI technology in business operations. 

 

The attendees share direct experiences, challenges, and approaches to optimizing product marketing, collaborative opportunities, and organizational efficiency. 

 

Several questions are explored regarding best practices and new tools for expanding product reach and improving operational workflow.

 

Introductions and Meeting Purpose
  • Prue confirms the agenda centers on TikTok strategy, business growth for 2026, and the shift in paid advertising away from Amazon.
  • Abe identifies his business as operating in the OTC pharmaceutical sector and seeks basic guidance on TikTok, noting he is an Amazon expert but a TikTok beginner.

 

TikTok Strategy for OTC Pharmaceuticals
  • Abe explains that his products fall within the $10 price range and considers creating mixed bundles to raise the ticket size.
  • Prue suggests creating a bundled kit, such as an at-home allergy emergency kit, to boost brand visibility and ticket value.
  • Prue shares her experience with TikTok, highlighting the importance of product testing on the platform and adapting based on traction.
  • Abe emphasizes that the goal is not necessarily virality but brand awareness on TikTok, which can influence Amazon sales.

 

TikTok Advertising and Content Approach
  • Prue insists that video content is essential for success on TikTok.
  • Jason Pratt joins, sharing his experience running TikTok ads directly to Shopify. He reports poor conversion rates on Shopify but significant indirect sales increases on Amazon.
  • Jason discusses challenges for sellers in Canada, such as lacking access to TikTok Shop, and alternatives like running ads linked to a Shopify store.
  • Prue and Jason advise focusing on video content and targeting specific product pain points, rather than broad, multi-purpose products, to improve performance on TikTok.
  • Jason warns against combining too many functions in a single product, using the example of a failed attempt to market a combined allergy and multivitamin product.
  • Jason suggests using creator-generated content boosted with ad spend and evaluates the compliance of titles and descriptions.

 

TikTok Boosting and Management Practices
  • Ozlem asks about campaign management on TikTok, specifically the practice of boosting individual videos versus using GMB Max.
  • Prue describes better results from boosting individual videos before employing automated tools like GMB Max.
  • Prue details hiring a “head of growth” with extensive experience, highlighting the impact on sales growth, video virality, and multi-platform sales. (No specific name, but the recruitment platform Jazz HR is mentioned.)
  • Participants discuss the use of platforms like Jazz HR (a recruitment software that integrates with LinkedIn) for hiring, focusing on candidates from Argentina or Colombia.

 

Off-Amazon Advertising and Affiliate Partnerships
  • Abe seeks advice on the next advertising channel after Amazon and Walmart. Jason recommends affiliate marketing and content partnerships, especially for products with regulatory challenges.
  • Prue recommends joining major affiliate networks, particularly those familiar with restrictive or regulated categories.
  • Jason shares a case study where cross-platform promotion via TikTok and Instagram, using Amazon Associates links, significantly increases sales.
  • Prue points out the success of affiliate-driven marketing using comment automation and Instagram partnerships.

 

AI Applications in E-commerce
  • Jan Krapp asks for examples where AI delivers substantial operational benefits beyond “nice to have” features.
  • Aiden Chien explains the use of AI in creating image and video content, yielding substantial cost reductions and operational efficiency.
  • Aiden references AI solutions popular in China for PPC ad management. He describes systems that automate ad targeting and reporting, freeing up human resources.
  • While successful in visual content and ad automation, Aiden notes his team has yet to fully embrace AI for organizational operations.

 

Closing Remarks and Upcoming Events
  • Prue shares information on upcoming e-commerce events in Miami, including eCom Boardroom, TikTok masterminds, Cosmoprof Miami, and MDS Centurion dinners. 
  • Jason Pratt seeks recommendations for invoice factoring partners for retail and is advised to reach out via Twitter and the ECF community.
  • Aiden Chien discusses the importance of regularly launching new products due to changes in Amazon’s algorithm, highlighting a strategic lesson about product and channel diversification.
  • Prue recommends the “From Grand Slams to Flatlines” episode of the Operators podcast (dated December 31, 2025, featuring Sean and Matt) as a valuable resource for learning about business diversification and risk management.
  • The meeting closes with remarks about maintaining innovation and diversity to avoid stagnation, and participants note contact offers, future follow ups, and meeting schedules.

 

In conclusion, this session thoroughly explores actionable techniques for e-commerce growth through platforms like TikTok, affiliate marketing, and AI technology. 

 

The participants stress the importance of content quality, targeted bundles, and strategic hiring to maximize brand reach and profitability. 

 

The conversation closes with guidance on leveraging both innovative and tested practices to stay competitive, alongside reminders about upcoming industry events and valuable media resources for continued learning.

items.title: How to Use Amazon Marketing Cloud to Beat Competitors with Smarter Marketing Strategies with Neha Bhuchar of Atom11
items.description:
In this session, Neha Bhuchar from Atom11 shares practical advice on building audiences, optimizing campaigns, and maximizing results through data-driven techniques.
TOPICS:
  1. Understanding and applying Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC) data
  2. Strategies for audience targeting and increasing conversions
  3. Practical frameworks and Q&A for campaign optimization
items.description_text: In this session, Neha Bhuchar from Atom11 shares practical advice on building audiences, optimizing campaigns, and maximizing results through data-driven techniques. TOPICS: Understanding and applying Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC) data Strategies for audience targeting and increasing conversions Practical frameworks and Q&A for campaign optimization
cliff_notes:
In this session Neha Bhuchar from Atom11 leads an in-depth presentation providing both conceptual understanding and actionable strategies for leveraging AMC to beat competitors and optimize campaigns on Amazon. 

The session includes practical tips, a demonstration of real-world scenarios, and a Q&A addressing category-specific nuances and AMC accessibility.

Introduction, Meeting Setup, and Background

  • Iliana informs attendees that the recording and presentation are available on the provider page for later reference.
  • Neha Bhuchar introduces herself as the co-founder of Atom11, an award-winning Amazon Ads automation software company.
  • Neha highlights her experience at Amazon, her contributions to Prime Video Ads, and her extensive background speaking at advertising industry events.

Understanding Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC)

  • Neha explains that AMC is essentially a large, anonymized Excel sheet that tracks each customer’s interactions with ads at the event level.
  • She emphasizes that each row in AMC represents a customer’s journey, detailing events such as viewing ads, clicking, or making purchases.
  • AMC allows advertisers to analyze customer data and create actionable audience segments without access to personal information.
  • The clean room structure of AMC protects customer privacy while enabling advertisers to gain deep data insights.

Analyzing AMC Data and Building Audiences

  • Neha describes how to use AMC data pivots to identify behaviors, such as customers who clicked ads but did not convert.
  • She explains that advertisers can create customer cohorts—for example, segmenting audiences by actions taken or time-to-purchase.
  • AMC enables targeting or bid-boosting ads to these specific audience cohorts for refined advertising strategies.


Strategic Use of AMC to Beat Competitors

  • Neha outlines three main strategies: increasing reach, boosting conversions, and enhancing basket size value.
  • She advises prioritizing ASINs (Amazon Standard Identification Numbers) based on key performance indicators such as “new to brand” and customer lifetime value.
  • She distinguishes between rule-based and lookalike audiences: larger brands benefit from rule-based audiences, while smaller brands with lower spends see better results with lookalike audiences.
  • She highlights the competitive benefit of targeting audiences who search for competitor keywords.

Sequential Targeting and Funnel Strategies

  • Neha demonstrates the sequential targeting strategy where different Amazon ad types (DSP, Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Products) are layered in a funnel.
  • She explains that creating touchpoints at each funnel stage significantly increases conversion rates, as demonstrated by client case studies.
  • The strategy, developed at Atom11, is cited as an award-winning, data-driven approach that increases campaign efficiency even at higher cost per click (CPC).

Utilization of Pre-Built and High-Performance Audiences

  • Neha recommends using Amazon’s pre-built audience called “highly likely to purchase based on shopping activity,” which consistently outperforms custom audiences in conversion rates.
  • She stresses the importance of leveraging this audience within automatic or broad campaigns to maximize campaign reach and results.
  • She provides examples where clients observed substantial gains from these intelligent audiences with minimal extra effort.


Retargeting High-Value Customers and Maximizing AOV

  • Neha explains methods to target and retarget high-value customers who previously purchased, using high average selling price (ASP) products to increase basket size.
  • She describes how to tailor look-back periods and retargeting windows based on product repeatability (e.g., short for laptops, long for tissue paper).
  • She underscores the importance of identifying and focusing on customers likely to generate high lifetime value for the brand.

Framework for Building Better Audiences

  • Neha presents a framework based on repeatability, suggesting high repeat products warrant longer look-back windows than low repeat, high-ticket items.
  • She provides real-world experimentation data showing that longer look-back periods yield better conversion and order results for highly repeatable products.
  • Audience segmentation and retargeting methods are refined for maximum relevance and return.

The session provides a comprehensive overview of Amazon Marketing Cloud and equips attendees with actionable insights for smarter audience segmentation, campaign optimization, and competitive strategy. 

Neha’s practical advice, from leveraging pre-built audiences to customizing retargeting based on product characteristics, gives brands a roadmap to improving their Amazon ad performance. 

Participants are encouraged to connect with Atom11 and utilize the shared resources to implement these strategies.

items.title: How Communication and Public Speaking Skills Drive Better Business Results and Profit with Alan Kishk
items.description:
In this session, participants practice their communication and public speaking skills through interactive exercises, sharing personal experiences, and receiving constructive feedback in a safe and encouraging environment.
  1. Public speaking techniques and practice
  2. Personal challenges and communication goals
  3. Feedback and strategies for improvement
items.description_text: In this session, participants practice their communication and public speaking skills through interactive exercises, sharing personal experiences, and receiving constructive feedback in a safe and encouraging environment. Public speaking techniques and practice Personal challenges and communication goals Feedback and strategies for improvement
cliff_notes:
In this session MDS Members gather to practice and enhance their communication and public speaking skills. The call features practical exercises, personal sharing, and feedback in a supportive, non-judgmental environment, led by Alan Kishk, who has extensive experience in teaching public speaking. 

 

Throughout the session, various techniques and topics are discussed, with each attendee contributing their perspectives and receiving individualized feedback.

 

Introductions and Goals
  • Jamie welcomes the group, explaining that this call is for practicing communication and public speaking skills. 
  • Alan shares his background as a public speaking mentor, leader of Toastmasters meetings, operator of a roofing company, and private coach for individuals ranging from students to professionals.
  • Alan stresses that he is passionate about public speaking because it enables personal transformation and achievement for himself and those he teaches.
  • The session’s primary purpose is to practice public speaking in a safe, supportive environment with the goal of personal and professional growth.

 

Personal Experiences in Public Speaking
  • Alan shares transformative stories from his clients: a once-shy lawyer who found confidence, obtained a promotion, and started a family, and a young, anxious student who blossomed after improving communication skills.
  • Participants discuss their own public speaking experiences. Jamie recounts his time at Toastmasters and notes his informal call-hosting experience.
  • Several attendees identify their communication challenges, including presenting clearly, managing feedback, and overcoming nervousness.

 

Session Structure and Rules
  • Alan emphasizes that the session is a "public speaking gym," where everyone can practice without fear of criticism or judgment.
  • He encourages participants to turn on their cameras for better engagement and explains that the meeting is interactive, with participants presenting brief speeches on assigned topics.
  • Alan clarifies that if anyone does not want to be recorded, Jamie will pause the meeting recording on request.

 

Interactive Practice and Participant Sharing
  • Participants are invited to share communication challenges and motivations for attending. Lisa expresses some uncertainty about her communication gaps. Mars describes difficulty delivering feedback delicately. June notes that communicating to a team with varied backgrounds is sometimes challenging. Ryan reveals his tendency to "beat around the bush" and lack clarity.
  • Jamie would like to present more clearly and compassionately in both professional and personal settings.
  • Alan uses positive reinforcement, reassuring participants that expressing care for others and self-awareness are strengths that support effective communication.

 

Practical Exercises and Feedback
  • Alan leads a series of practice speeches, assigning participants to respond to specific questions within a 60-second time frame.
  • Jamie practices a business pitch, and Alan provides feedback on his structure, comfort, and areas of improvement, particularly the importance of focusing on the listener's needs and managing time.
  • Ryan presents the proudest moment of his career and receives feedback on his clarity and staying within the time limit; Alan encourages emotional engagement and more vivid storytelling.
  • June answers a scenario question about motivating a burnt-out team member, demonstrating empathy and structured communication. Alan commends her for her organization, sensitivity, and pace.
  • Alan shares an acronym, "SPEAKER," to encapsulate seven public speaking skills: Structure, Pace, Emotion, Audible (clarity and volume), Know your Audience, Eye contact, and Rest in Peace (eliminate filler words like "um" and "uh").

 

Theoretical Insights and Additional Resources
  • Alan discusses the importance of self-assessment and non-critical self-improvement after every speaking opportunity.
  • He introduces "the three cardinal rules" for communication: All actions should serve the purpose of delivering the message effectively; the communicator should build authority and worthiness; and helping others is the root purpose of communication.
  • Alan shares a personal anecdote about empathy in leadership, demonstrating how respecting personal circumstances builds organizational trust.
  • Book names, email addresses, and specific websites are not mentioned in the meeting. However, Toastmasters International and Regis (a provider of flexible office spaces) are discussed as organizations relevant to the context.

 

Handling Specific Challenges
  • June asks for advice on overcoming anxiety when speaking to larger groups versus being interviewed one-on-one. Alan recommends preparation, practice, and applying the "SPEAKER" acronym.
  • Ryan brings up imposter syndrome and questions of worthiness, to which Alan and June both offer supportive perspectives. Alan reinforces that incremental practice and a willingness to be corrected lead to growth and acceptance.
  • The session concludes with Alan motivating everyone to embrace their learning journeys and consistently apply the discussed techniques for both speaking and listening.

 

Throughout this session, participants actively engage in sharing challenges, practicing key techniques, and providing feedback in a genuinely supportive forum. 

 

The session not only imparts actionable frameworks like the "SPEAKER" acronym and the cardinal rules but also nurtures empathy, confidence, and continuous learning. 

 

By fostering open dialogue and practical exercises, the group demonstrates the importance of safe spaces for self-improvement and the long-term transformation that practice and reflection can bring to communication and public speaking.
